method: Paired 60-second replay of the Rate card with its one-card lookahead. The control chooses familiar, informative questions. The variant selects a familiar question with expected value for the best three of a bounded shortlist, from 3 through 19 completed ratings. Each arm starts with the same empty profile and saved quiz seed. A rating costs 4 assumed seconds and an unseen answer costs 2.
split: Held-out viewers, with 30% of their ratings withheld (at least 10, at most 1000), as prepared by scripts/refinement_inputs.py. Films withheld for grading cannot be asked about. Their ratings are absent from the question policy.
measure: Among viewers reaching three ratings in both arms, compare the share of the three graded picks rated at least 4 stars. Each arm grades its own highest-scoring held-out films with at least 2,000 IMDb votes, using the same match ranking and eligibility rule. Additional outputs include the three-rating threshold, observed cards and per-viewer yield with unready viewers counted as zero.
interval: Paired mean difference plus or minus 1.96 standard errors across evaluable viewers. Metric values are proportions.
scope: The replay uses historical ratings of previously watched films, catalog build 20261116194147, and a simulated time budget. It assesses cold-start Rate cards before visiting Home. Human timing, post-recommendation watches and the poster-wall experience require prospective evaluation.
reproduceValidation: python scripts/refinement_inputs.py --split val --users 400 | node scripts/compare_quiz.mjs --data site/data
reproduceTest: python scripts/refinement_inputs.py --split test --users 5000 | node scripts/compare_quiz.mjs --data site/data

validation400.metric: Historical 4+ among three popular withheld films; simulated Rate-card time

test5000.metric: Historical 4+ among three popular withheld films; simulated Rate-card time

rollout: The validation and held-out estimates differ in direction, and the held-out interval includes zero. Ordinary quiz behavior stays the default. Settings offers an opt-in, on-device randomized comparison.
